content.text: No exclusivity or sole-source obligation binding IBM appears anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, MSL agrees to produce and sell, and IBM agrees to purchase Products. This Agreement does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product.
input.rationale: This meets the preferred position: nothing binds IBM to buy exclusively or to source solely from MSL. Scope of Work (§3.0) covers only "selected manufacturing, Integration, and other Services", and the SOW purchase clause (§6.0) is a generic purchase commitment driven by Purchase Orders, with no "exclusive", "sole supplier", "all of its requirements" or "shall not procure from any third party" language anywhere in the Base Agreement, SOW, or attachments. The agreement in fact assumes IBM's freedom to move volume elsewhere — §9.0(e) expressly contemplates "reductions of Products requirements due to migration to a competitive supplier". The only sole-source style restrictions run against MSL (e.g. IBM Nominated Suppliers, Prohibited Suppliers at §16.15, and IBM Parts used solely in IBM Products), which benefit us and are not flagged. Any volume/forecast commitments are addressed under MINCOMMIT rather than double-flagged here.
